newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti debt soars over two months period.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti debt soars over two months period.

text.p: Italy's troubled information and technology group Olivetti said on Monday its net group debt had nearly doubled in July and August due to seasonal payments to suppliers and heavy restructuring costs.

The company, under financial scrutiny by official bodies and analysts, said its debts had soared to 2.39 trillion lire ($1.6 billion) at the end of August from some 1.26 trillion lire at the end of June.

The loss-making hi-tech group confirmed that its net first half 1996 loss was 440.2 billion lire, but added further financial details in the two months of July and August to satisfy official investigations into its financial accounts.

The group said in a detailed 150-page statement that its debt has increased due to the seasonality of debt level in paying suppliers, on-going restructuring costs and investments into its 41.3 percent-owned Omnitel mobile phone consortium.
Olivetti also gave details of its commercial credit arrangement putting operations on securitisations of debts at 344 billion lire and factoring at 321 billion lire out of its total group debt level.

Despite the sharp rise in debt levels and the confirmation of a 200 billion lire restructuring charge in the first half, the group said it saw the potential for a better operating result in the second half of 1996 compared to the first half.

Olivetti published its first half 1996 results in early September but on the very next day its director general in charge of finance and auditing Renzo Francesconi resigned after he cast doubts on the accuracy of its first half results.
After an initial inquiry by Consob, the stock market watchdog demanded further information and especially on its July and August period after the first-half had closed.

Olivetti said that the group's sales trend during these two months had continued in line with that seen in the first half. In this period sales slipped 11 percent to 4.22 trillion lire as the group slumped to an operating loss of 80.8 billion from a operating profit of 73.4 billion the previous first half.

Olivetti said that its publication gave all the details that Consob had demanded in its 16 questions put to it, with many analysts focusing on the company's level of in-debtness before trying to assess the company's ability to recover.

The group is set to meet industry analysts in Milan and London on October 3 and October 4 where its new chief executive Roberto Colaninno will try to soothe the nerves of its long suffering shareholders. ($1=1,522 lire)
